MY LITTLE SCIENCE PROJECT

My Bean Leaf

Become a leaf detective. Look gently and leave the leaf attached to the plant.

Start with the outline, then look at the tip, edge and veins. Use descriptive words such as broad, pointed, smooth or bumpy. You do not need to pick the leaf to make a detailed drawing.

With a grown-up: use untreated planting beans; do not eat seeds or sprouts. Keep small seeds away from younger children. Wash hands after handling. An adult should discard any mouldy setup.

Read the complete activity guide ↗
LOOK · THINK · TRY

Explore before you start.

Careful observation uses more than a quick glance. Describing shape, colour and texture helps us notice similarities and differences.

Look at the picture, talk about what you notice, then use the drawing and writing spaces below. Open the picture for a closer look.

Start with the outline

Follow the edge with your eyes. Is the tip pointed? Is the leaf broad or narrow? Draw the outside shape before adding details.

Look for veins

Veins form a branching pattern through the leaf and carry materials. Draw the strongest middle line, then add the smaller ones you can actually see.

Compare gently

Two leaves on one plant can be different sizes. Keep them attached and compare their colour, outline and texture without bending or tearing them.

Use a finger, stylus or mouse in each drawing box. Type below it, or ask a grown-up to write your words. Your work stays in this tab. Save before refreshing or leaving.

ACTIVITY 1

Look and draw

Draw the outside shape of a leaf. Add any lines you can see.

ACTIVITY 2

Describe your leaf

With a grown-up, gently touch a safe leaf on your bean plant. Wash your hands afterward.

ACTIVITY 3

Look again later

Observe the same leaf on another day, or compare it with a different leaf.

Your ideas belong here. There is no score.

What are we learning?

Careful observation uses more than a quick glance. Describing shape, colour and texture helps us notice similarities and differences.
